meta.project: Bilingual, Ontology-Aware, and Explainable ESG Intelligence System
meta.description: Integrated research synthesis mapping 5-layer ESG objectives to technical contributions and empirical literature evidence from the EMNLP/ACL 2025 dataset.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: It's All About In-Context Learning! Teaching Extremely Low-Resource Languages to LLMs
literature_references.authors: Yue Li, Carolina Scarton, Zhi-xue Zhao
literature_references.relevance: Provides empirical evidence for C3 and RQ1.1 by demonstrating that zero-shot ICL with language alignment is effective for acquiring extremely low-resource languages without PEFT, specifically where scripts are under-represented.

literature_references.title: A Case Against Implicit Standards: Homophone Normalization in Machine Translation for Languages that use the Ge'ez Script
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ1.3 by analyzing how normalization affects linguistic understanding in under-represented scripts, justifying the need for the regional calibration strategies proposed in C1.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?

literature_references.title: DCIS: Efficient Length Extrapolation of LLMs via Divide-and-Conquer Scaling Factor Search
literature_references.authors: Lei Yang, Shaoyang Xu, Deyi Xiong
literature_references.relevance: Directly justifies C13 and RQ2.2 by introducing a divide-and-conquer search for scaling factors to extend context windows efficiently, addressing the scalability problems (P4) identified in the plan.

literature_references.title: Persona-Augmented Benchmarking: Evaluating LLMs Across Diverse Writing Styles
literature_references.relevance: Supports C8 by demonstrating how diverse writing styles impact benchmark scores, necessitating the robust representation learning and multi-model benchmarking proposed.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Thread: A Logic-Based Data Organization Paradigm for How-To Question Answering with Retrieval Augmented Generation
literature_references.relevance: Causally supports C7 and RQ3.2 by introducing 'logic units' to transform documents into structured representations, enabling more coherent and transparent reasoning chains.

literature_references.title: Sparse Autoencoder Features for Classifications and Transferability
literature_references.relevance: Justifies C15 and RQ3.1 by providing a framework for extracting interpretable, ontology-aligned features from LLM activations to improve transparency.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.2: How can cross-model consistency be measured?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: The Stepwise Deception: Simulating the Evolution from True News to Fake News with LLM Agents
literature_references.relevance: Provides the causal logic for C11 and RQ4.5 by modeling how truthful narratives are gradually distorted, offering a simulation framework for detecting greenwashing.

literature_references.title: Attacking Misinformation Detection Using Adversarial Examples Generated by Language Models
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ4.1 and C14 by identifying how adversarial rephrasings can bypass detectors, validating the need for the plan's tone-aware bias correction.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: CheckEval: A reliable LLM-as-a-Judge framework for evaluating text generation using checklists
literature_references.relevance: Operationalizes RQ5.1 and C5 by providing a checklist-based framework that decomposes criteria into traceable binary decisions for auditable outputs.

literature_references.title: A Position Paper on the Automatic Generation of Machine Learning Leaderboards
literature_references.relevance: Supports C12 and RQ5.2 by advocating for standardized, automatically generated leaderboards to ensure system scalability and research extensibility.
